relevance_note: In scope because the paper reports individual clinical detail for people with the disease ('Case Reports of 23 New Patients'; 'The clinical features of 23 patients (20 fam ilies) with SSADH deficiency'), although it prints no ALDH5A1 variant for any of them.
method_note: Worked by hand from the Markdown full text; no script transcribed any table or text. The paper has one table ('TABLE. Clinical Findings in 23 Patients With Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency'), converted as two blocks. Block 1 was used for age at diagnosis (all 23 patients), sex and ethnicity, quoting the row from the patient label through the cell. Block 2 is badly OCR-corrupted (merged rows 'B.H. C.S.' and 'P.V.l TA.', garbled labels 'i.e.', 'U S ,', 'J.LY.1I'), so it was not used at all. The legend defines only '*' (MRI/CT), a dagger (first cousins), a symbol for presenting signs, a section symbol (see Case Reports) and bars (siblings); it never defines '+' or '-', so no table symbol was read as evidence: consanguinity is recorded only where the case report states it, and is 'not reported' for C.S., D.E., J.E.Y., J.I.Y., K.S., P.F., P.S. and P.V. even though their cells hold '-' or '+'. Stacked cells ('D.E. | + + / - section' for seizures, 'J.E.Y. | + / - section' for hypotonia, 'N.O. | + / - section' for ataxia) were not assigned to anyone by position (D-31). Contradictions, all left 'not reported' in the checklist and reported in phenotypic_features only where both statements are individual-level: B.E. walks with an 'unsteady gait' yet 'did not show ataxia or hypotonia'; I.C. had a 30-word vocabulary but did not combine words while the Discussion calls his speech and language normal; N.O. has pallidal hyperintensity in the text while block 2 says 'MRI probably normal?'; T.A. had 'Two EEGs and MRI were normal' while cranial CT 'raised the ques- tion of cerebellar atrophy'. P.S.H.'s age at death is 13 years in the Methods and 13!/2 years in her own case report. K.S. is not a contradiction (normal MRI in 1992; globus pallidus, thalamus and brain-stem lesions in February 1996). D.E.'s hedged 'He may have had a few very short astatic seizures' was not counted as observed in the checklist. The Discussion's 'exemplified in A.R, in whom the correct diagnosis was not achieved until 25 years of age' is taken to be the 25-year-old patient A.F., not a further person, because the paper calls him 'only the second adult patient'. The paper hyphenates words across PDF line breaks with an invisible soft hyphen (U+00AD) followed by a space; such spans are written with \u00ad and are verbatim. No ALDH5A1 variant is printed anywhere: the gene appears only as 'The SSADH gene is single copy and has been mapped to chromosome 6p23.7', no molecular testing of patients is reported, and every diagnosis rests on urinary organic acid analysis plus enzyme activity, so no variant is tied to any person and the variants table is empty. is_proband is false for everyone with a null span: no person is called the proband or index case (the only occurrence is the cohort phrase 'Approximately 40% of the probands in this report'). Ages printed in garbled OCR form ('3V2 y', '4 ]/2 y', '9lA y', '6% y', '13l/2 years', '7Vi years') were kept verbatim with a null ISO 8601 value. Labels use the paper's own initials; K.S. is taken from the case report although the table prints 'ICS.'. Relatives: the three relatives for whom the paper gives an individual-level fact got rows (the mother of P.S.H., the maternal sister of I.C., the paternal cousin of I.C.); relatives described only as healthy or well, or only as a group ('three siblings who are well', 'two older, healthy siblings', 'an older sister who is healthy', 'a healthy, older male sibling', 'two other children, a 16-year-old and a 14-year-old, who were healthy'), got no rows, because the paper gives no individual-level clinical fact about any of them - a judgement call. The previously published Algerian patient of the Discussion (reference 5) got a row because the paper gives his sex and origin. HPO candidate labels and IDs were left null.
